summary.text: Tyler Davis, a no-party-affiliation candidate, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Florida's 1st Congressional District to Jimmy Patronis.
Describing herself as a woman and mother, she says she has worked in the financial industry for more than a decade and founded the nonprofit A Pensacola Perspective.

paragraphs.text: Davis graduated from Tate High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Pensacola State College in 2017, according to Ballotpedia.
Ballotpedia lists her profession as artist, while in her own words she has worked in the financial industry for more than a decade.

Davis founded and operates A Pensacola Perspective, a nonprofit focused on volunteerism, civic engagement, and local partnerships, which she says brings together residents, businesses, nonprofits, educators, and local governments.
Ballotpedia lists her as disqualified in the 2025 special election for this seat, and she was on the November 3, 2026 ballot as a no-party-affiliation candidate.
During the campaign, she said she was running to give Northwest Florida a representative who listens and works with local communities.
She received 1.8% of the vote to Jimmy Patronis's 62.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
